title: Diffusion Domain
outOfScope: Stage assignment, stage transition, scoring, ranking, threshold distance, reporting, scheduling, persistence, and delivery
Automatic inference that one observation proves industry adoption, productivity improvement, or a reference model
External source adapters, network/database/LLM integrations, cross-feature imports, and new dependencies

sources.reason: Repository operating rules and validation requirements.
Canonical Work Item and governance terminology.
Layer direction and Domain isolation rules.
Diffusion is an evidence dimension, not an automatic score.
Reference-model boundary and explicit evidence discipline.
Traceable facts, polarity, and missing-proof boundary.
Competitor imitation and industry diffusion validation concepts.
Predecessor boundary that must not be imported by Diffusion Domain.

riskAssessment.reason: Diffusion facts can be over-read as proof of industry-wide adoption. The Domain must retain explicit observations and categories without inferring a stage or score.
riskAssessment.reviewNotes: Source acquisition, cross-company identity resolution, persistence sufficiency, stage recommendation, and ranking remain deferred.

reasons: Diffusion Domain code, tests, and evidence require the standard governed review route.

executionDecision.reason: The explicit user authorization covers execution and Contract recording for all 24 roadmap Work Items.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: Diffusion Domain exposes CompetitorImitation with subject company, imitator company, scope, and observation date retained as explicit facts.
Diffusion Domain exposes JobTaxonomyChange, BenchmarkObservation, and IndustryDiffusion facts with stable identities and insertion-order collections.
DiffusionProfile rejects blank required values and duplicate identities while preserving the supplied observation order.
DiffusionSignalKind distinguishes workflow redesign, job taxonomy, productivity benchmark, advisory adoption, and capital reallocation without assigning a score or stage.
The Domain remains independent of infrastructure, interface, network, database, LLM, external source, and other feature modules.
Focused unit and integration tests cover imitation, taxonomy, benchmark, industry diffusion, duplicate rejection, order preservation, and no-inference behavior.
The design spec and execution plan record the diffusion boundary, no-goals, authorization, current-WI issue rule, and verification commands.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Keep Diffusion Domain independent of external systems and other feature modules.
Retain diffusion facts as evidence; do not infer stage, score, ranking, or industry adoption from one fact.
Preserve explicit company identities, dates, descriptions, and collection order.
Do not add dependencies for this Contract.
Resolve issues within the current Work Item when they remain inside its Contract scope; open a successor only for a distinct or materially expanded boundary.
Do not introduce trading, price prediction, or capital-action behavior.

intent.problem: The repository has no typed Diffusion Domain for competitor imitation, job taxonomy change, benchmark facts, or industry diffusion observations.
constraints: Retain supplied diffusion identities, company references, descriptions, dates, categories, and benchmark comparisons without calculating adoption or productivity conclusions.
Keep competitor imitation, job taxonomy, benchmark, and industry diffusion as distinct explicit facts; do not collapse them into a score or stage.
Diffusion Domain stays provider-agnostic. Use existing Rust conventions. No cross-feature imports.
intent.rationale: A pure Diffusion model gives later Stage Gate, Ranking, Reporting, and Weekly Radar WIs auditable diffusion facts while preventing unsupported claims of industry adoption.
